import pandas as pd

# File paths for source CSVs
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_58/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_58/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_58/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_58/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_58/training_4.csv",
]

# Read all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first index column
dfs = [pd.read_csv(f, index_col=0) for f in source_files]

# Concatenate all source tables (UNION)
df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# The 'Year' column is like "2010 (83rd)" - extract the number inside parentheses as integer year
# According to target examples, 'Year' is integer like 84, 42, 85 etc.
# The number inside parentheses is the ordinal number of the ceremony, e.g. 83rd -> 83
# But target examples show years like 84, 42, 85 which correspond to ceremony number (not calendar year)
# So we extract the number inside parentheses and convert to int

df['Year'] = df['Year'].str.extract(r'\((\d+)[a-z]{2}\)').astype(int)

# The columns 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner' in source are strings, but target expects integers.
# From intermediate_step1 examples, these columns have integer values equal to the 'Year' column.
# The target examples show Nominee, Movie, Winner columns have the same integer values as Year.
# So we set Nominee, Movie, Winner columns to be equal to Year column as integers.

df['Nominee'] = df['Year']
df['Movie'] = df['Year']
df['Winner'] = df['Year']

# The 'Category' column is already string and matches target schema.

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
df = df[['Category', 'Year', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']]

# Save the final target table to the specified path
df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_58/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read all source CSV files with index_col=0
df0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_58/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_58/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_58/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
df3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_58/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
df4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_58/training_4.csv", index_col=0)

# UNION all source tables (concatenate)
df = pd.concat([df0, df1, df2, df3, df4], ignore_index=True)

# Group by 'Category' (primary key) and aggregate counts of other columns
result = df.groupby('Category').agg(
    Year=('Year', 'count'),
    Nominee=('Nominee', 'count'),
    Movie=('Movie', 'count'),
    Winner=('Winner', 'count')
).reset_index()

# Ensure columns are in the exact order as target schema
result = result[['Category', 'Year', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']]

# Write to target CSV
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_58/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
